subject: Pilot insurance buffer vs top-up purchase — pricing counterproposal
messages:
From: Sasha Kline <sasha.k@veridian.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short pilot — surge insurance vs one-off top-up?

Marcus — thanks again for the demo last week. The team has one blocker: our pilot is trending higher-than-expected on token usage during ingestion tests. We have two asks: 1) can Redwood offer a short "surge insurance" buffer (a small pool of emergency credits that kicks in if we exceed the pilot cap), or 2) would Veridian be better off buying a top-up pack of tokens/days at a discount?

We prefer the insurance approach (keeps things simple), but procurement needs a clear dollar table to compare to a standard top-up purchase. Can you send a concise counterproposal with pricing and the mechanics (how it applies, expiration, and whether it converts into committed credits if we convert to a paid plan)? Also, we may need a short extension (5–7 days) if we opt for the insurance while we run the final ingestion.

Thanks — Sasha
Sasha Kline
Product Ops Manager, Veridian Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Kline <sasha.k@veridian.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — surge insurance vs one-off top-up?

Hi Sasha — appreciate the clear ask. Drafting a short counterproposal below; attaching a 1-page runbook and a pricing worksheet for the two options. See also the HubSpot deal link in the footer if you want the proposed amendment draft.

Option A — Surge insurance buffer (recommended for low-friction ops)
- Buffer: 100k generation tokens reserved as "insurance" for the remainder of the pilot
- Price: $1,200 flat (one-time, applied immediately)
- Mechanics: buffer only charges if you exceed the pilot cap; it will auto-apply at overage moment and reduce future overage invoices
- Expiration: 30 days from purchase or when pilot converts to paid account (whichever is earlier)
- Convertibility: If Veridian converts to a committed plan within 60 days, 75% of unused buffer value can be applied as a one-time credit toward the first committed invoice

Option B — Top-up token pack (explicit purchase)
- Pack: 200k generation tokens
- Price: $2,000 one-time
- Mechanics: consumed first, does not depend on exceeding cap; no auto-apply later
- Expiration: 90 days
- Convertibility: non-convertible (standard top-up)

Counterproposal notes and trade-offs:
- Insurance gives lower up-front spend and easier procurement sign-off for short experiments; it supports a 5–7 day extension to the pilot at no additional cost if the buffer is purchased (we'll add an amendment).
- Top-up is cleaner for finance if preferred as a pre-paid asset; larger upfront discount if you need longer runway.

Attachments: pilot_runbook_v2.pdf (implementation + SLOs) and proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx (line-item math).

If this looks sensible, I can loop in Contracts for a short amendment and route a DocuSign link. Priyom — can Finance confirm whether the insurance is okay to appear as a one-time service line vs prepay in Veridian's PO?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — surge insurance vs one-off top-up?

Thanks Marcus — quick finance note: for enterprise procurement teams, the distinction matters. If Veridian needs the buffer to be capitalized on their books, they'll push for the top-up (prepaid). If they accept it as a service line (expense), surge insurance works and is simpler to invoice.

Operational asks: if we do the insurance route, add the following limits to the amendment: 1) single auto-apply per pilot (no repeated triggers), 2) cap on per-token effective rate to avoid surprise invoices if ingestion spikes massively, and 3) a log export to Veridian's S3 detailing when buffer was consumed. Marcus — I can add the standard finance/legal language and loop Contracts after Sasha confirms.

Priyom Das
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Sasha Kline <sasha.k@veridian.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@veridian.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — surge insurance vs one-off top-up?

Marcus/Priyom — thanks, that framing helps. Procurement prefers prepaid packs for accounting, but product wants the insurance buffer because it's lower friction. Proposed middle ground: we take the insurance buffer now (100k tokens at $1,200) and agree to convert 50% of any unused buffer credit to committed credits if we sign a 12-month commit within 45 days. That gives procurement some capitalization optionality because they can choose to prepay the conversion at conversion time.

We also confirm we need a 7-day extension to the pilot window to run the final ingestion; please include that in the amendment. If you can get a DocuSign by end of week, procurement will route the PO promptly.

Sasha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Kline <sasha.k@veridian.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — surge insurance vs one-off top-up?

Perfect — glad we found a compromise. Next steps: 
1) I'll update the pricing worksheet to reflect Sasha's tweak (insurance buffer $1,200; 50% unused convertibility toward a 12-month commit if signed within 45 days).
2) Laura, can you and Contracts prepare a 7-day pilot amendment that: lists the buffer mechanics, the single-trigger rule, per-token cap at $0.015 effective rate for buffer consumption, S3 log export, and the convertibility clause (50% unused conversion)?
3) I'll send the DocuSign envelope and HubSpot deal update (link attached).

Sasha — you'll see the DocuSign link as soon as Contracts publishes it; if procurement needs an alternate invoice flow (prepay vs service line), include that in the PO and we'll mirror the line-item.

Thanks — I'll own the execution this week.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
